predictions.title: Disaggregated prefill ships as vLLM and SGLang serving default by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 9 disaggregated-prefill convergence forces prefill/decode disaggregation out of the Cloudflare-Infire-specific edge architecture and into the documented default serving mode shipped by vLLM and SGLang at the H100 and L40S tiers. The catalysts landing across a single weekend cycle are concrete and mutually reinforcing: vLLM v0.11.1 ships a disaggregated-prefill mode that, per Cloudflare Infire engineering's Saturday benchmark note, reaches parity with the production Infire edge architecture on prefill throughput at the H100 tier, with Infire retaining only a 1.4x advantage at the L40S edge tier on decode-side latency rather than the order-of-magnitude gap that previously kept disaggregation out of the open-source serving stack; the Yotta Labs benchmark refresh holds the canonical shared-prefix workload at approximately 14,650 tok/s on vLLM versus 17,300 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk, narrowing the throughput gap to a level where the architectural choice (monolithic vs disaggregated) dominates the remaining delta; SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 ships a parallel architectural primitive in the form of RadixAttention-aware tool-result-cache reuse delivering a 2.1x speedup on tool-calling-heavy agentic workloads, demonstrating that the radix-tree cache substrate generalizes from prefix sharing to tool-call result sharing; and Trail of Bits's full red-team write-up on SGLang RadixArk CVE-2026-44567 (CVSS 8.1 authenticated server-side template injection) plus the v0.11.1 patch for the prefix-cache poisoning CVE-2026-44512 disclosed Friday convert the security narrative from a blocker to a documented disclosure-timeline pattern. The structural force is that once Cloudflare Infire engineering publishes a benchmark showing parity at the H100 tier between its production edge architecture and an open-source serving stack's disaggregated mode, downstream framework maintainers can cite the production-comparable benchmark rather than ship monolithic-mode defaults, and the SGLang radix-tree cache substrate gives a parallel architectural lineage that converges on the same shape. The most likely shape is a disaggregated-prefill/decode mode added as the documented default in the vLLM v0.12 and SGLang RadixArk v0.6 release lines, with per-tier deployment templates targeting H100 single-node and L40S edge-tier topology, plus a Yotta-style canonical benchmark harness gating the production-readiness claim. Sovereign-cloud and on-prem agentic-AI workloads adopt it first because the tool-result-cache reuse substrate compounds the latency win for long tool-call chains. Bear case is a competing serving-stack architecture refusing the disaggregation split and forking the benchmark methodology; absent that, Q4 2026 lands disaggregated prefill as the documented default across the open-source serving cohort.

reasoning.because: May 9 Cloudflare Infire benchmark: vLLM v0.11.1 disaggregated prefill hits H100 parity vs Infire.
reasoning.given: SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 ships 2.1x speedup on tool-call workloads; vLLM 14.65k vs SGLang 17.3k tok/s.
reasoning.so_that: vLLM, SGLang RadixArk, and Cloudflare Infire all ship disaggregated prefill/decode as documented default mode.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; H100 + L40S edge tiers; Yotta benchmark refresh as gating evidence.
reasoning.plain_language: Cloudflare proved vLLM matches its production speed when split into a prefill and decode stage, so other serving tools will copy the split.

predictions.summary: Cloudflare Infire benchmarks vLLM v0.11.1 disaggregated prefill at H100 parity with Infire production edge; Infire keeps a 1.4x decode edge at L40S. SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 adds tool-result-cache reuse. By Q4 2026 disaggregated prefill ships as documented default in vLLM and SGLang.

predictions.title: Mistral Workflows tenancy clause enters EU central-government RFPs by Q1 2027
predictions.body: By Q1 2027 the May 9 Mistral AI Workflows day-nine sovereign-cloud landing — France's Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) selecting Workflows for tax-return anomaly-detection routing across the central tax-administration estate with the Workflows control-plane separation architecture plus sovereign-cloud execution-worker model explicitly named as procurement deciders over LangGraph self-hosted plus the Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 registry, paid Workflows tenancy lifting to 296 enterprise customers (vs 290 Friday) with daily-execution count crossing 4.4M, and the parallel Workflows-Codestral integration note showing per-step token-budget bookkeeping interoperates with the OpenAI Codex CLI /agent Plan-Apply mode export format — combined with the May 8 BNP Paribas Securities Services + Siemens Healthineers + Saudi Aramco Digital go-live cohort that lifted tenancy past 290, the Singapore IMDA / Japan AISI cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter now extended to South Korea PIPC + New Zealand GCSB inside the May 9 weekend extension, and the NHS England agentic-AI workflow-platform CVE blocklist naming LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 + LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188 + CrewAI CVE-2026-44352 + Haystack CVE-2026-44391 as disallowed pre-patch versions — force the next wave of EU central-government and allied-jurisdiction AI-orchestrator RFPs to name a Workflows-shaped sovereign-cloud tenancy clause (control-plane separation between tenant data and orchestrator runtime, sovereign-cloud execution-worker model with named-jurisdiction execution boundary, per-step token-budget bookkeeping interoperable with the OpenAI Codex CLI export format) as a baseline procurement-eligibility requirement rather than a discretionary scoring criterion. The forcing function is that once a flagship central-tax-administration estate cites the architecture by name as the decider against the two leading US alternatives, EU member-state procurement frameworks and Indo-Pacific reciprocity signatories have a defensible reference template they can require without authoring bespoke language. The most likely shape is a four-jurisdiction cohort (France DGFiP-equivalent + Germany BSI-equivalent + at least one Singapore/Japan signatory + at least one Five Eyes ally) treating sovereign-cloud control-plane separation plus execution-worker jurisdiction plus token-budget interop as the paired clauses; sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt first because the AISI-administered cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter is already the operative threshold. Bear case is that AWS Bedrock Agent Registry's FedRAMP-Moderate inheritance plus the Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center reciprocity-attestation field add ships a hyperscaler-managed sovereign-cloud equivalent first; absent that, Q1 2027 lands the Workflows-shaped tenancy clause across the cohort.

predictions.summary: Mistral Workflows lands DGFiP's central tax estate May 9 with sovereign-cloud control-plane separation cited as decider over US alternatives. By Q1 2027 EU + allied AI-orchestrator RFPs name the Workflows-shape sovereign-cloud tenancy clause as eligibility.

predictions.title: FMRB executive order adopts allied cyber-eval reciprocity ladder by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the White House Frontier Model Review Board executive-order draft now circulating in interagency review (OSTP press-pool confirmation that no signing window opens before May 22, May 15 14:00 EDT S-407 classified threshold briefing with NIST Director Locascio, the ODNI cyber lead, and a CISA Joint Cyber Defense Collaborative representative attending, AI Policy Institute plus R Street plus Public Knowledge plus Lawyers for Civil Justice plus the Knight First Amendment Institute plus EFF coalition pressing a documented State Farm reasoned-decision record and a 60-day Defense Production Act Section 708 public-comment window) combined with the weekend extension of the Indo-Pacific cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter (South Korea PIPC plus Ministry of Science and ICT formal-mirror signal, New Zealand GCSB observer commitment with Q3 2026 mirror, layered on the May 7 EU AI Office plus UK AISI memorandum-of-cooperation and the May 8 Singapore IMDA plus Japan AISI parallel MoC with Canada CCCS plus Australia ASD ACSC observers) forces the signed FMRB executive order to incorporate an allied cyber-evaluation reciprocity ladder naming the EU AI Act Section 51 regime, the UK AISI voluntary frontier-model program, and the Indo-Pacific Singapore plus Japan plus South Korea cohort as the operative satisfying surface for the FMRB's 30-day pre-release notification requirement, with AISI-administered TLO-range runs treated as reciprocal evidence inside a 120-day placement window and per-tenant Mythos-class capability attestation logs (the May 9 arxiv 2605.05933 leakage-freedom proof plus Anthropic Project Glasswing primitive) named as the compliance-evidence shape. The forcing function is that the litigation-vector that AI Policy Institute and the Knight-EFF amicus letter have crystallized cannot be answered with DPA Section 708 voluntary information-sharing language alone; the EO drafters need a multilateral reciprocity anchor that gives the comment-window response a procedural floor and the State Farm record an evidentiary baseline, and the EU-UK-Indo-Pacific cohort is already operationally aligned around AISI's 32-step The Last Ones range. The likely shape is a named-jurisdiction reciprocity annex to the EO with the four already-signed regimes plus the South Korea mirror plus the New Zealand observer ladder, tied to the May 21 CISA federal-civilian KEV-mirroring cadence as the operative review tick. Bear case is the EO ships unilateral first and bolts on reciprocity via OSTP letter exchange; absent that, the signed EO lands the ladder inside Q3 2026.
